_voice: Informal "ti". Avoid gendered past-tense verbs for the user or partner where possible.
_style: Always address the user informally with “ti” (tvoj, tebi, te) and verbs in 2nd person singular; address the couple as “vas dvoje” with 2nd person plural (“vaše stablo”, “posadite”), never formal “Vi”. The other person is “partner” only in short labels and section titles; in running text prefer the name placeholder or “voljena osoba”, and never use dečko/cura, muž/žena, partnerica or slash forms like “spreman/spremna”. Croatian past tense (l-participle) and adjectives mark gender, so for the user or the partner rephrase with present tense (“%@ ti piše”, “Želiš li sigurno izbrisati…?” instead of “Jesi li siguran?”), passive/impersonal forms (“Pismo je poslano”, “Zaliveno zajedno”), nouns (“Dobrodošlica!” or “Dobro došli” for the couple) or imperatives. A partner’s name placeholder (%@) is NEVER declined and never takes a case ending: keep it in nominative subject position or set it off with a colon or dash (“%@ ti šalje sjeme”, “Pismo – %@”, “Od: %@”), never “od %@-a” or “s %@om”. Quotes are Croatian „ ” outside and ‚ ’ inside; apostrophe ’; ellipsis is the single character …; dash is an en dash – with spaces; no space before ? ! : ; and keep “ · ”, \n and emoji exactly as in the source. Numbers use a decimal comma and a dot (or non-breaking space) for thousands (1.250; 4,5); dates are written “14. 11. 2026.” or “14. studenoga 2026.” with months lowercase in the genitive, ordinals take a dot (“3. godišnjica”), times are 24-hour (21:30). Plural categories are one / few / other: one = 1, 21, 31… (“%lld dan”), few = 2–4, 22–24… (“%lld dana”), other = 0, 5–20, 25… and decimals (“%lld dana”); always fill all three. Buttons and short actions use the 2nd person singular imperative as on iOS (“Spremi”, “Odustani”, “Pošalji pismo”, “Pokušaj ponovno”); titles, tabs, chips and buttons use sentence case (capital on the first word only), except proper names like Coupley, Premium and CoupleSync. Use Latin script with full diacritics (č ć đ š ž), ijekavian standard Croatian (“vrijeme”, “dijeliti”, “uspomena”), Croatian rather than Serbian/Bosnian vocabulary (“tjedan”, “kruh”, “obavijest”, “sigurnosna kopija”), and keep “veza” for the relationship: network connection is always “internetska veza” and disconnecting partners is “odspojiti”, never “prekinuti vezu” (which means breaking up). Tone: warm, light and natural, never cheesy or overly formal.
partner: partner (u rečenici radije ime ili „voljena osoba”)
